title: Israel election: Netanyahu-led bloc in slight lead with more than half of votes counted
summary: While partial results show the pro-Netanyahu bloc ahead of the anti-Netanyahu bloc, the final tally could take days. Neither grouping is expected to win a majority, with tough coalition talks ahead.…
byline: Patrick Große, Mark Hallam, Felix Tamsut, Roshni Majumdar, Matt Ford

image.caption: An election billboard of the Democrats party featuring Yair Golan and othersImage: Nir Elias/REUTERS

blocks.text: Left-wing leader calls for 'courage' to unite with Arab parties

blocks.caption: An election billboard of the Democrats party featuring Yair Golan and othersImage: Nir Elias/REUTERS

blocks.text: Yair Golan, the head of Israel's main left-wing party, the Democrats, has called on partners in the opposition alliance to be ready to work with Arab parties to gain a majority and take government.
"We must no longer accept [Prime Minister Benjamin] Netanyahu's racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes," he said on X.
"We have a responsibility. And we have an opportunity to form a government of change in partnership with Israel's Arab citizens," he wrote.

Arab parties have around 16 seats amid the ongoing count, while the anti-Netanyahu bloc under former military chief Gadi Eisenkot is on around 48, meaning that a coalition between them would produce the necessary majority in the Knesset.
Netanyahu's bloc had some 56 seats after around two-thirds of votes had been counted.
Several opposition parties have so far rejected working together with the Arab parties.
